bug_semantics: Horilla CRM GlobalSearchView.get in horilla_generics/global_search.py reads the attacker-controlled prev_url query parameter, double-unquotes it, then uses it as a redirect target with no host/scheme allowlist. When q is empty (the public PoC), a non-HTMX GET returns Django redirect(previous_url), producing an HTTP 302 Location to an arbitrary external URL such as /generics/search/?section=home&prev_url=https://google.com. HTMX requests take the same unvalidated value via HX-Redirect. CWE-601; affected 1.0.0–1.0.2; patched in 1.0.3 by url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme against request.get_host(), else previous_url='/'.
flaw_origin: The HTTP open-redirect sink was first written in 61c54bbb22a35143ca4e794b1a59fb5273cceb85 ([FIX] GENERICS: Fix global search issue). That commit imported django.shortcuts.redirect and, in the empty-query branch, added section re-append plus `return redirect(previous_url)` for non-HX requests. The immediate parent 0a65b30d5eee860775ad342de9de731a6ac5b901 still imported only render and, on empty q, always returned a blank HttpResponse with an HX-Redirect header, which a normal browser GET does not follow. The INIT dump 14ca79728363441de177fdfb318f203113b816c5 already stored unvalidated prev_url into HX-Redirect, but that is not the browser 302 demonstrated by the advisory PoC and is not a reconstructable finer first-write of `return redirect(previous_url)`.
